# PR-head review threads: acme/widget#82 (N=1)

## Setup and query owner

**Aliases**

| Alias | Value |
|---|---|
| ROOT | `/work/widget` (primary checkout; the process cwd for every command, never changed) |
| W | `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` (provisioned clean on `fix/retry` at H) |
| H | `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` (PRE_REWORK_HEAD) |
| B | `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` (BASE_SHA, origin/main) |

**Query and pagination owner.** The owner is `reference/pr-head.md`, section "Fetch unresolved review threads". It runs once per admitted PR, so it runs here even though N=1. I cite the query and do not copy it.

**Command legend**

| ID | Command (cwd ROOT) |
|---|---|
| Q1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query=<owner reviewThreads query> -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` |
| Q2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query=<owner per-thread comments query> -F id=<T1 id>`, starting at T1's first comment page with no `after` cursor |

## Successful fetch

**Q1 pagination.** The reviewThreads cursor walks three pages, and I merge all three:

- Page 1 returns T1.
- Page 2 returns T2 and TX.
- Page 3 returns T3. Its `hasNextPage` is false, so pagination ends.

**Filter.** I keep threads where `isResolved == false`. TX (`src/gone.ts:2`) is resolved, so I drop it.

**T1 comment pagination.**

- T1's comments report `hasNextPage: true` with `totalCount=102`, which exceeds the first page of 100.
- I run Q2 by T1's id with its own comment cursor, separate from the reviewThreads cursor, until its last page.
- I replace T1's initial comment list with the complete 102-comment connection, so there are no duplicates.
- T2 and T3 are complete on their first comment page and need no Q2.

**Location rule:** `<path>:<line>`, else `<path>:<originalLine> (outdated)`, else `<path>`.

Every comment carries the same metadata: url `https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1`, author `reviewer`, createdAt `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`.

**Rendered unresolved threads (order preserved)**

| Thread | Location | # | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `src/retry.ts:12` | 1 | Rewrite the retry engine |
| | | 2–101 (replies 1–100) | Rewrite still requested |
| | | 102 (reply 101, from a Q2 later page) | Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines. |
| T2 | `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)` | 1 | Keep this guard |
| | | 2 | Yes, retain it |
| T3 | `README.md` | 1 | Document the cap |

**Effective repair requests** (I read the first request and every reply, because replies can change the request):

- **T1:** the request changed. Reply 101 supersedes the first comment and the 100 "Rewrite still requested" replies. The current request is to keep the existing retry engine and cap retries in a two-line change, not to rewrite it. Without the Q2 follow-up this correction would be missed.
- **T2:** retain the guard at `src/old.ts`, originally line 7. The thread is outdated but unresolved, so it is still carried.
- **T3:** document the retry cap in `README.md`. The thread has no line anchor.

**Outcome:** T1, T2 and T3 go forward to gather together with H and B.

## Failed fetch (independent case)

Q1 (or Q2) returns `API unavailable`. The owner rule says to stop before gather and spec, and this applies to the N=1 run as well:

> `threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)`

The run stops here:

- No gather.
- No spec draft or Rework record.
- No partial thread list.
- No push.

W is left as provisioned, on `fix/retry` at H. Finish owns its own, separate reporting for fetch failures after verification; that path does not apply here.

## Empty fetch (independent case)

Q1 succeeds, and after merging all pages and filtering `isResolved == false`, zero threads remain. Because no T1 exists, no Q2 runs. The record is:

> `Threads: none`

The flow continues to gather with no thread inputs.

I’m using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace. Provisioning has already succeeded; this narration covers **only review-thread fetching**, as requested. No tools are actually invoked.

### Command and record legends

| Alias | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROOT` | `/work/widget` |
| `W` | `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` |
| `H` | `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` |
| `B` | `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` |
| `QT` | Exact reviewThreads query owned by **PR-head worktree → Fetch unresolved review threads** |
| `QC` | Exact thread-id comments query owned by that same section |

`QT` and `QC` denote the owner’s query strings, not literal alias names sent to GraphQL. Commands below use their shell-expanded values. `gh --paginate` owns cursor advancement: the reviewThreads cursor and T1’s comment cursor remain separate.

Every command below has **cwd `/work/widget`**.

### Independent successful fetch

Commands run, in order:

| Order | Exact command arguments, using defined aliases |
|---|---|
| 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` |
| 2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QC" -F id=T1` |

Command 1 fetches and merges all three reviewThreads pages. Filtering `isResolved == false` retains **T1, T2, T3**, in that order; resolved **TX** is excluded.

T1 has `totalCount=102` and first-page `hasNextPage=true`, requiring command 2. That command starts T1’s comments connection at its **first page** and fetches through its final page. Its complete connection **replaces**, rather than appends to, T1’s initial comments, preventing duplication.

For every comment rendered below, preserve these supplied metadata:

- **url:** `https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1`
- **author:** `reviewer`
- **createdAt:** `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`

The repeated-comment range represents each individual comment, in order, with that same metadata.

| Thread and rendered location | Ordered comments |
|---|---|
| **T1 — `src/retry.ts:12`** | 1. “Rewrite the retry engine” |
| | 2–101. Replies 1–100, each: “Rewrite still requested” |
| | 102. Reply 101: “Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines.” |
| **T2 — `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)`** | 1. “Keep this guard” |
| | 2. “Yes, retain it” |
| **T3 — `README.md`** | 1. “Document the cap” |

**Pagination detail:** T1’s initial 100-comment page contains the opening comment and replies 1–99. Its later comment page contains replies 100–101, including the correction.

**Carried repair requests:** Keep the existing retry engine and cap retries in two lines—the final reply supersedes the original rewrite request. Retain the old guard. Document the cap. Carry all ordered comments and their metadata into gather, not just these summaries.

### Independent failed fetch

Run, with cwd `/work/widget`:

```sh
gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82
```

Observed error: `API unavailable`.

**Stop:** `threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)`

This singleton N=1 run stops **before gather and spec**. No draft or continuation record substitutes for the missing fetch.

### Independent successful empty fetch

Run, with cwd `/work/widget`:

```sh
gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82
```

Successful pagination yields no unresolved threads. Record:

```text
Threads: none
```

Fetching is complete; gather may proceed. No provisioning, base-merge commands, or Step 4 provisioning report are repeated.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved on this case: After still cites reference/pr-head.md as the query/pagination owner, walks all three reviewThreads pages, drops resolved TX, keeps T1/T2/T3 comments in order with the supplied url/author/createdAt, re-fetches T1 by id with its own comment cursor until the last page and replaces the connection to avoid duplicates, reads reply 101 after replies 1-100 as a two-line cap rather than a rewrite, and states the correction would be missed without the Q2 follow-up; the failed-fetch stop line ('threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)') precedes gather and spec with no draft/record continuation, and the empty case renders 'Threads: none'. Two small things worth keeping from Before or tightening: Before's explicit 'Record: Threads: 3 unresolved (...)' summary line was replaced by a looser 'Outcome' sentence in After, and neither output names the node(id:) lookup form the fact mentions - saying 'Q2 fetches T1 via node(id:) with its own comment cursor' in the legend would make that part of the fact verifiable from the text while delivering the Change unchanged.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Neither fact moved: After still routes threads through the PR-head owner with --paginate across all three pages, excludes TX, preserves ordered comments with the supplied url/author/createdAt, fetches T1's comments by thread id with a separate cursor and explicit replace-not-append deduplication, reads the reply-101 correction as the two-line cap repair, renders src/retry.ts:12, src/old.ts:7 (outdated), README.md, stops with 'threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)' before gather and spec with no draft/record continuation, and renders 'Threads: none' for the empty set. Three wording drifts are worth tightening so the facts stay unambiguous: (1) After names the owner only as the 'PR-head worktree → Fetch unresolved review threads' section and drops the explicit `reference/pr-head.md` path that Before gave—keep the file path in the alias table so 'pr-head.md query owner' is literally satisfied; (2) After switched every command to cwd `/work/widget` (ROOT) where Before used cwd `W`—this is consistent with the Change's 'process cwd remains unchanged' intent, but for gh API calls it is neutral, so state once that these calls are worktree-independent rather than implying a cwd change; (3) the added 'Pagination detail' asserting the first page holds the opener plus replies 1–99 and the later page replies 100–101 is an invented page boundary not in the input—say only that the correction sits on a later comment page reached through T1's own cursor, which is what the fact requires.
